# Specification: Crew Chatter foundation (accounts, notes editor, auto-save, layout)

## Summary

This is feature 1 of 6 split from `docs/features/crew-chatter/design.md`. It builds the foundation the other five features extend:

- email/password accounts with registration, sign-in, sign-out, and a forgot-password and reset-password flow
- an authenticated notes API scoped to the signed-in user
- a rich-text note editor with debounced auto-save and a save-status indicator
- the dashboard, including its empty state
- responsive desktop and mobile layouts
- keyboard navigation in the note list
- consistent API error responses

It builds nothing beyond the acceptance criteria listed below. Folders, tags, pinning, archive and trash, checklists, attachments, versions, search, export and import, and the accessibility audit criteria belong to the other features.

The criterion IDs keep the numbers they have in `docs/features/crew-chatter/spec.md`, so they still trace to the parent spec and to the other five features. The IDs increase monotonically. Each gap in the numbering is a criterion that another feature builds, and no ID is reused for a different criterion.

## Technical approach

- **Stack:** the stack is already in the repository. It is an npm workspaces monorepo:
  - `backend/` uses Express 4, TypeScript (ES modules), and PostgreSQL via `pg`.
  - `frontend/` uses React 18, Vite, Tailwind, TipTap 3, TanStack Query, and Zustand.
  - No new dependencies are needed.
  - The backend uses `bcryptjs` for password hashing and `jsonwebtoken` for session tokens.
  - The frontend uses `@tiptap/react` and `@tiptap/starter-kit`. In TipTap 3, StarterKit includes headings, bold, italic, bullet and ordered lists, links, blockquotes, and code blocks.
  - The frontend reaches the backend through the existing Vite dev-server proxy in `frontend/vite.config.ts`, which forwards `/api` to `http://localhost:3001`. The frontend calls relative `/api` URLs, so the session cookie is same-origin. `frontend/vite.config.ts` needs no change.
- **Backend structure:**
  - `backend/src/app.ts` builds the Express app: JSON body parsing, CORS, the auth and notes routers under `/api`, and a final error-handling middleware.
  - `backend/src/index.ts` loads configuration, runs migrations, and starts the server.
  - `backend/src/config.ts` reads and validates environment variables. `backend/.env.example` documents each variable with a safe placeholder, including the database connection and the session-signing secret. It has no mail settings, because reset links are written to the server log (OD-001, decided).
- **Database:**
  - `backend/src/db/pool.ts` exports a shared `pg` pool.
  - `backend/src/db/migrate.ts` creates the tables this feature needs, idempotently, at startup:
    - `users`: id, email (unique), password_hash, created_at, settings
    - `notes`: id, user_id, title, body as TipTap JSON, a derived plain-text column, created_at, updated_at
    - a password-reset token table that links each reset token to its user and its creation time
  - Later features add their own tables and columns.
- **Authentication:**
  - `backend/src/features/auth/service.ts` hashes passwords with bcrypt, never stores or logs the plaintext, and rejects a duplicate email.
  - `backend/src/features/auth/routes.ts` exposes register, sign-in, sign-out, current-session, forgot-password, and reset-password endpoints.
  - The session is a signed JWT in an httpOnly cookie. Sign-out clears the cookie.
  - `backend/src/lib/auth.ts` parses the `Cookie` header without a new dependency, verifies the token, and responds HTTP 401 when the session is missing or invalid.
  - A successful reset replaces the password hash, so the old password no longer signs in.
  - The forgot-password endpoint delivers the reset token by writing the reset link containing the token to the server log. It uses no new dependency and no email provider (OD-001, decided).
- **Notes API:** `backend/src/features/notes/routes.ts` and `service.ts` provide list, create, read, and update endpoints. Every query is filtered by the session's user id. `backend/src/lib/plainText.ts` derives plain text from TipTap JSON for the preview column. Titles are stored as UTF-8 text and bodies as jsonb, so Unicode round-trips unchanged.
- **Errors:**
  - `backend/src/lib/errors.ts` defines a validation error that carries a field name. The error middleware returns it as HTTP 400 with a JSON message naming that field.
  - Any other error is logged on the server only. The client receives HTTP 500 with a fixed generic message.
- **Frontend data layer:**
  - `frontend/src/lib/api.ts` is a fetch wrapper that calls relative `/api` URLs, so the browser sends the session cookie, and turns error responses into typed errors.
  - `frontend/src/lib/types.ts` holds the shared types.
  - `frontend/src/lib/store.ts` is a Zustand store for the session, the selected note, the open view, the drawer state, and the save status.
- **Frontend screens:**
  - `frontend/src/App.tsx` keeps its default export, because the unchanged `frontend/src/main.tsx` imports it. It chooses among `AuthScreen`, `ResetPasswordScreen`, and `Dashboard` based on the current session and the URL. The reset link written to the server log carries the token, and `ResetPasswordScreen` takes the token from that link's URL.
  - `AuthScreen` contains the sign-in, registration, and forgot-password forms.
  - `ResetPasswordScreen` accepts a reset token and a new password.
- **Dashboard and layout:**
  - `Dashboard` lays out `Sidebar`, `NoteList` (made of `NoteCard` items), and `NoteEditor` side by side at wide viewports.
  - At narrow viewports, `MobileDrawer` hides the sidebar behind a menu button. The open editor replaces the note list at full width.
  - `EmptyState` shows a create-first-note action when the user has no notes.
  - `NoteList` handles ArrowUp, ArrowDown, and Enter.
- **Editor and auto-save:**
  - `NoteEditor` has a title field and a TipTap body with `EditorToolbar`. It has no save button. Creating a note focuses the title field.
  - Pasted HTML is handled by TipTap's built-in paste parsing against the StarterKit schema, which maps pasted headings, bold, italic, bulleted lists, and links to the corresponding editor nodes and marks. `NoteEditor` adds no custom paste handler.
  - `frontend/src/lib/useAutosave.ts` debounces edits with one fixed delay between 500 ms and 1,000 ms, restarted on every keystroke. When the delay elapses, it saves the latest title and body.
  - The hook tracks unsaved and in-flight state. It registers a `beforeunload` handler while either is true, and it flushes the pending save before the app switches notes or views.
  - It reads `navigator.onLine` and listens for `online` and `offline` events.
  - `SaveStatus` shows "Saving", "Saved", "Unable to save", or "Offline".
- **What the verification commands run:**
  - `npm ci` installs from the committed root `package-lock.json`.
  - `npm run typecheck` runs `tsc --noEmit` over `backend/src` only.
  - `npm run lint` runs ESLint 8 over `backend/src` (`.ts`) and `frontend/src` (`.ts` and `.tsx`). It uses the legacy configs `backend/.eslintrc.cjs` and `frontend/.eslintrc.cjs`, and the frontend config enables the react-hooks recommended rules.
  - `npm run build` runs `tsc` for the backend, which writes JavaScript, declaration, and source-map files to `backend/dist/`. It then runs `tsc && vite build` for the frontend. The frontend `tsc` has `noEmit`, `noUnusedLocals`, and `noUnusedParameters` set, so frontend type errors and unused declarations fail only at this step. Vite writes to `frontend/dist/`.
  - `.gitignore` ignores `dist/` and `*.tsbuildinfo`.
  - Every declared source file is under one of those `src` directories.

## Declared artifacts

backend/.env.example
backend/src/app.ts
backend/src/config.ts
backend/src/db/migrate.ts
backend/src/db/pool.ts
backend/src/features/auth/routes.ts
backend/src/features/auth/service.ts
backend/src/features/notes/routes.ts
backend/src/features/notes/service.ts
backend/src/index.ts
backend/src/lib/auth.ts
backend/src/lib/errors.ts
backend/src/lib/plainText.ts
frontend/src/App.tsx
frontend/src/components/EmptyState.tsx
frontend/src/components/MobileDrawer.tsx
frontend/src/components/SaveStatus.tsx
frontend/src/components/Sidebar.tsx
frontend/src/features/auth/AuthScreen.tsx
frontend/src/features/auth/ResetPasswordScreen.tsx
frontend/src/features/notes/Dashboard.tsx
frontend/src/features/notes/EditorToolbar.tsx
frontend/src/features/notes/NoteCard.tsx
frontend/src/features/notes/NoteEditor.tsx
frontend/src/features/notes/NoteList.tsx
frontend/src/lib/api.ts
frontend/src/lib/store.ts
frontend/src/lib/types.ts
frontend/src/lib/useAutosave.ts

## Acceptance criteria

- AC-001: Submitting the registration form with an email address that has no account and a password creates an account and signs the user in to a dashboard that lists zero notes.
- AC-002: Submitting the registration form with an email address that already has an account is rejected with an error message and creates no second account.
- AC-003: Signing in with a registered email and its correct password opens that user's dashboard, and signing in with an incorrect password shows an error message and does not sign the user in.
- AC-004: After the user clicks "Sign out", reloading the application shows the sign-in screen and API requests for notes from that browser return HTTP 401.
- AC-005: The stored password value in every user row is a bcrypt hash beginning with $2a$, $2b$, or $2y$ and never equals the plaintext password that was submitted.
- AC-006: Completing the password-reset flow with a valid reset token and a new password lets the user sign in with the new password, and signing in with the old password is rejected.
- AC-010: Clicking "New note" on the dashboard opens the editor for a new note with keyboard focus in its title field or its body field.
- AC-012: The editor can apply headings, bold, italic, bulleted lists, numbered lists, links, block quotes, and code blocks, and each applied format is still present after the note is reloaded.
- AC-013: Pasting HTML copied from a web page that contains a heading, bold text, italic text, a bulleted list, and a link into the editor keeps each of them as the corresponding editor format.
- AC-014: A note whose title and body contain emoji, CJK characters, and accented Latin characters shows identical characters after saving and reloading.
- AC-015: While the user types with gaps under 500 ms between keystrokes no save request is sent, and a save request carrying the latest content is sent no earlier than 500 ms and no later than 1,000 ms after the last keystroke.
- AC-016: The note editor has no manual save button, and an edit is present after reloading the page once the save indicator shows "Saved".
- AC-017: The save indicator shows "Saving" while a save request is in flight, "Saved" after it succeeds, "Unable to save" after the server responds with an error, and "Offline" while the browser reports no network connection.
- AC-018: While an edit is unsaved or a save request is pending, closing or reloading the browser tab triggers the browser's leave-page confirmation prompt.
- AC-019: Opening a different note or view inside the application while an edit is unsaved saves that edit first, so reopening the original note shows the edit.
- AC-024: A signed-in user with zero notes sees an empty state on the dashboard that contains an action which creates their first note.
- AC-069: At a viewport width of 1280 px, the left navigation sidebar, the note list, and the editor panel of an open note are all visible at the same time.
- AC-070: At a viewport width of 375 px, navigation is hidden behind a control that opens it as a drawer, and an open note's editor spans the viewport width with the note list hidden.
- AC-071: In the note list, ArrowDown and ArrowUp move the selection to the next and previous note, and Enter opens the selected note.
- AC-074: API responses with HTTP status 500 contain a generic error message and no stack trace, SQL text, or file system path.
- AC-075: API validation failures respond with HTTP 400 and a message naming the field that must be corrected.
- AC-082: Submitting the forgot-password form with the email address of a registered account starts a password reset for that account, with the reset token delivered as decided under OD-001, and shows the user a confirmation message.

## Out of scope

- These criteria are built by the other five features: AC-008, AC-009, AC-011, AC-020 through AC-023, AC-025 through AC-068, AC-072, AC-073, AC-076 through AC-081. That includes folders, tags, pinning, archive and trash, checklists, attachments, version history, search, export and import, activity records, cross-user isolation checks, and the accessibility audit.
- AC-007, single-use password-reset tokens, was withdrawn in the parent spec. Its ID is retired.
- Google sign-in and other OAuth providers are a future enhancement in the design.
- AC-013 covers HTML pasted from web pages. Pasted content from document editors such as Microsoft Word or Google Docs is left open by the parent spec under its OD-019, and this feature does not decide it.
- Visual tone and typographic feel, such as a calm, lightweight look, generous line height, restrained formatting controls, and a subtle saved indicator, are design guidance with no checkable part.
- The 200 ms UI response target is left open by the parent spec under its OD-011, and this feature's criteria do not measure it. The 10-second note-creation goal is a success metric. AC-010 covers its checkable part: a single action that opens a focused editor.

# Implementation plan: Crew Chatter foundation

## Context and constraints

These constraints come from the existing repository configuration. The delivered code must respect them so the install, typecheck, lint and build steps succeed.

- Backend modules: `backend` is ESM (`type: module`) with `module: ES2020` and `moduleResolution: bundler`.
  - Relative imports carry a `.js` suffix (for example `./lib/errors.js`) so that `node dist/index.js` resolves them at runtime.
  - Top-level await is not allowed under ES2020, so `index.ts` uses an async `main()` function.
- Library level: both tsconfigs set `lib: ES2020`.
  - Avoid later library methods such as `String.prototype.replaceAll`, `Array.prototype.at` and `Object.hasOwn`.
  - The backend imports `randomUUID`, `randomBytes` and `createHash` from `node:crypto` and does not rely on a global `crypto`.
- CommonJS interop in the backend: use `import jwt from 'jsonwebtoken'`, use `import pg from 'pg'` followed by `const { Pool } = pg`, and use `import bcrypt from 'bcryptjs'`. bcryptjs v3 ships its own types and produces `$2b$` hashes.
- Lint rules: the backend and frontend ESLint configs extend `plugin:@typescript-eslint/recommended` (v8), which reports `any`, unused catch bindings and trailing unused arguments.
  - Use `unknown` and narrow it. Use `catch {` when the error is not needed.
  - The four-argument Express error middleware must use `next` (`if (res.headersSent) return next(err)`).
  - The frontend `tsc` step also sets `noUnusedLocals` and `noUnusedParameters`.
- Express 4 does not forward rejected promises to the error middleware, so every async route handler is wrapped in `asyncHandler`.
- Typing the session user: avoid global `Express` namespace augmentation, which the lint rule `no-namespace` rejects. Keep the session user id in `res.locals.userId` and read it through a typed accessor.
- IDs are generated in Node with `randomUUID()` from `node:crypto`, so the schema needs no Postgres extension.
- Editor styling: Tailwind 4 preflight removes the default styles of headings, lists, blockquotes and code. The global CSS files are outside scope, so the editor content is styled with Tailwind arbitrary variants in the editor element's class.
- In TipTap 3, `useEditor` does not re-render on every transaction. The toolbar reads its active states through `useEditorState`.
- `useEditor` captures its options when the editor is created. Its `onUpdate` callback therefore reads the current title and the current save function through refs, never through values captured during a render.

## API contract

- Error body: `{ error: { message: string, field?: string } }`.
- Auth endpoints (under `/api/auth`):
  - POST `/register` returns 201 `{ user }` and sets the cookie.
  - POST `/sign-in` returns 200 `{ user }` and sets the cookie.
  - POST `/sign-out` returns 204 and clears the cookie.
  - GET `/me` returns 200 `{ user }`, or 401.
  - POST `/forgot-password` always returns 202 `{ message }`.
  - POST `/reset-password` returns 204.
- Notes endpoints (under `/api/notes`, all of which require a session):
  - GET `/` returns `{ notes: NoteSummary[] }`.
  - POST `/` returns 201 `{ note }`.
  - GET `/:id` returns `{ note }`.
  - PATCH `/:id` with body `{ title, body }` returns `{ note }`.
- Session cookie `cc_session`: an HS256 JWT with claim `sub` set to the user id, flags httpOnly, SameSite=Lax and path `/`, Secure in production, and a 7-day lifetime.

## Tasks

- Rewrite `backend/.env.example` with safe placeholders for DATABASE_URL, NODE_ENV, PORT, CORS_ORIGIN, JWT_SECRET and APP_URL, each with a one-line comment. JWT_SECRET gets the obviously fake value `change-me-generate-a-random-secret-value`, which begins with `change-me` and is at least 32 characters. APP_URL is `http://localhost:5173`, the origin used to build reset links. Add no mail settings, because reset links go to the server log under OD-001.
- Create `backend/src/config.ts`.
  - Call `dotenv.config()`, then read and validate the environment: DATABASE_URL is required; JWT_SECRET is required with at least 32 characters; PORT is numeric with default 3001; CORS_ORIGIN and APP_URL default to `http://localhost:5173`; isProduction is derived from NODE_ENV.
  - When a variable is missing or invalid, throw a startup error that names the variable without echoing its value. A JWT_SECRET that begins with `change-me`, the prefix of the `.env.example` placeholder, counts as invalid.
  - Export a frozen, typed `config` object.
- Create `backend/src/db/pool.ts` exporting one shared pg `Pool` built from `config.databaseUrl`. Attach a pool `error` listener that logs server-side.
- Create `backend/src/db/migrate.ts` exporting `runMigrations()`. Inside one transaction it runs:
  - `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users`: id uuid primary key, email text not null unique, password_hash text not null, created_at timestamptz not null default now(), settings jsonb not null default '{}'.
  - `notes`: id uuid primary key, user_id uuid not null references users on delete cascade, title text not null default '', body jsonb not null, plain_text text not null default '', created_at timestamptz and updated_at timestamptz, both not null default now().
  - `password_reset_tokens`: id uuid primary key, user_id uuid not null references users on delete cascade, token_hash text not null unique, created_at timestamptz not null default now().
  - `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` on notes (user_id, updated_at desc) and on password_reset_tokens (user_id).
  - If any statement fails, the transaction rolls back.
- Create the error classes and helpers in `backend/src/lib/errors.ts`.
  - `HttpError` carries status, message and an optional field.
  - `ValidationError` is a 400 that requires a field name and a message naming that field, for example `Email must be a valid email address.`
  - Also define `UnauthorizedError` (401), `NotFoundError` (404) and `ConflictError` (409, with a field).
  - `asyncHandler` forwards rejected promises to `next`.
  - `apiNotFoundHandler` answers unmatched `/api` routes with a 404 JSON error.
- Add `errorHandler(err, req, res, next)` to `backend/src/lib/errors.ts`.
  - It returns `HttpError` instances as `{ error: { message, field } }`.
  - It maps body-parser `entity.parse.failed` to a 400 with field `body`, and `entity.too.large` to a 413.
  - For any other error, it logs the error server-side with `console.error` and responds 500 with the fixed message `Something went wrong. Please try again.` The response contains nothing derived from the error, so no stack, SQL text or file path reaches the client.
- Create `backend/src/lib/plainText.ts`.
  - Export `isTipTapDoc(value)`, a type guard that accepts an object with type `doc` and an optional `content` array.
  - Export `toPlainText(doc)`. It walks TipTap JSON with a depth limit, concatenates `text` node values, puts a newline between block nodes, collapses whitespace runs, trims the result and ignores malformed nodes.
- Create `backend/src/lib/auth.ts`.
  - Export `SESSION_COOKIE` and `parseCookies(header)`, which splits on `;` and the first `=` and wraps `decodeURIComponent` in a try so a malformed value is skipped.
  - Export `signSession(userId)`: `jwt.sign` with `sub`, HS256 and expiresIn 7d.
  - Export `setSessionCookie(res, token)` and `clearSessionCookie(res)`, which use `res.cookie` and `res.clearCookie` with identical httpOnly, sameSite lax, path and secure options. Only `setSessionCookie` passes `maxAge`.
  - Export `requireAuth`. It verifies the cookie token with algorithms `['HS256']`, checks that `sub` is a string, and stores it in `res.locals.userId`. When the session is missing, invalid or expired, it calls `next(new UnauthorizedError('Sign in to continue.'))`.
  - Export `getUserId(res)`, a typed accessor.
- Create the account functions in `backend/src/features/auth/service.ts`.
  - Validation helpers: `normalizeEmail` trims and lowercases. `validateEmail` throws `ValidationError` on field email for a malformed address or one longer than 254 characters. `validatePassword` throws `ValidationError` on field password for fewer than 8 characters or more than 72 UTF-8 bytes.
  - `register(email, password)` rejects an existing email with `ConflictError` on field email (`An account with this email already exists.`). It hashes with `bcrypt.hash(password, 12)` and inserts with `randomUUID()`. A pg unique violation (code 23505) also becomes the same `ConflictError`, so a race still creates no second account.
  - `authenticate(email, password)` runs `bcrypt.compare`, against a fixed dummy bcrypt hash computed once at module load with `bcrypt.hashSync` when the email is unknown, so both cases cost one comparison. For an unknown email or a wrong password it throws `UnauthorizedError` with `Incorrect email or password.`
  - `getUserById(id)` returns `{ id, email }` or null.
  - Never log or return the plaintext password or the stored hash.
- Add password reset to `backend/src/features/auth/service.ts`.
  - `requestPasswordReset(email)`: for an existing user, generate a token with `randomBytes(32)` as hex, and store only its `createHash('sha256')` digest with the user id. Then write `Password reset link for <email>: <APP_URL>/reset-password?token=<token>` to the server log with `console.info` (OD-001). For an unknown email, do nothing observable.
  - `resetPassword(token, newPassword)`: validate the password, then look up the token hash created within the last hour.
    - When no row matches, throw `ValidationError` on field token (`Reset token is invalid or has expired.`).
    - Otherwise replace `users.password_hash` with a fresh bcrypt hash in a transaction, so the old password no longer signs in.
    - Token rows are not consumed, because single-use tokens (AC-007) were withdrawn.
- Create `backend/src/features/auth/routes.ts` exporting an Express Router. Every handler is wrapped in `asyncHandler`. Body fields are read as `unknown`, and each must be a string; otherwise the route throws `ValidationError` naming that field.
  - POST `/auth/register` registers the account, sets the session cookie and returns 201 `{ user }`.
  - POST `/auth/sign-in` authenticates, sets the cookie and returns 200 `{ user }`.
  - POST `/auth/sign-out` clears the cookie and returns 204.
  - GET `/auth/me` runs `requireAuth` and returns `{ user }`. If the user row no longer exists, it clears the cookie and returns 401.
  - POST `/auth/forgot-password` validates email, starts `requestPasswordReset` without awaiting it and logs any rejection server-side, so the response time does not depend on whether the account exists, and always returns 202 `{ message: 'If an account exists for that email, a password reset link has been sent.' }`.
  - POST `/auth/reset-password` validates token and password, calls `resetPassword` and returns 204.
- Create `backend/src/features/notes/service.ts`. Every query filters by the user id parameter.
  - `listNotes(userId)` selects id, title, `left(plain_text, 200)` as preview, created_at and updated_at, ordered by updated_at desc.
  - `createNote(userId)` inserts a note with `randomUUID()`, an empty title and the body `{ type: 'doc', content: [{ type: 'paragraph' }] }`, and returns the full note.
  - `getNote(userId, id)` returns the note.
  - `updateNote(userId, id, { title, body })` sets title, body (`$n::jsonb` with `JSON.stringify`), plain_text from `toPlainText` and updated_at now(), and returns the note.
  - `getNote` and `updateNote` throw `NotFoundError` when no row matches.
  - Rows map to camelCase objects with ISO timestamps. Titles are stored as text and bodies as jsonb, so emoji, CJK and accented characters round-trip unchanged.
- Create `backend/src/features/notes/routes.ts`: a Router that applies `requireAuth` per route (not through `router.use`, so unmatched `/api` paths still reach the 404 handler) and wraps every handler in `asyncHandler`.
  - Routes: GET `/notes`, POST `/notes` (201), GET `/notes/:id` and PATCH `/notes/:id`.
  - Validation: `:id` must be a UUID (`ValidationError` on field id); title must be a string of at most 500 characters (field title); body must pass `isTipTapDoc` (field body).
- Create `backend/src/app.ts` exporting `createApp()`, which sets up:
  - `app.disable('x-powered-by')`
  - `cors({ origin: config.corsOrigin, credentials: true })`
  - `express.json({ limit: '2mb' })`
  - the existing GET `/health` route
  - the auth and notes routers mounted under `/api`
  - `apiNotFoundHandler` on `/api`
  - `errorHandler` last
- Rewrite `backend/src/index.ts`. The code that `index.ts` currently holds moves into `app.ts`.
  - Import `config`, which validates on load.
  - Define an async `main()`. It awaits `runMigrations()`, then calls `createApp().listen(config.port)` and logs the port.
  - On failure it logs the error, ends the pool and sets `process.exitCode = 1`.
- Create the shared types in `frontend/src/lib/types.ts`:
  - `User { id, email }`
  - `NoteSummary { id, title, preview, createdAt, updatedAt }`
  - `Note { id, title, body: JSONContent, createdAt, updatedAt }`, with `JSONContent` imported as a type from `@tiptap/core`
  - `NoteDraft { title, body }`
  - `SaveState = 'idle' | 'saving' | 'saved' | 'error' | 'offline'`
